Entered as second-class matter in the post office at New York City.

regions.label: plain_text
regions.text:
The June number of THE CRISIS will be a special Education number for Teachers. It will contain contributions by G. S. Dickerman, H. O. Tanner, W. S. Braithwaite. An important article on Harriet Beecher Stowe, by her son, C. E. Stowe. Our circulation is growing rapidly, but we must have 25,000. Every reader of THE CRISIS can by personal solicitation help us to this goal. Probably no magazine in America has a more interesting set of readers—we have on our books judges, financiers, philanthropists, college presidents and scholars, besides the best educated colored people of the country.

COMMENTS ON THE CRISIS

"Personally I have been so well pleased with your publication that I have not been able to keep a single copy, but have mailed them to friends

"I simply want to say that your April CRISIS is all in all the best document of its length on the color question that I have ever read."

regions.label: plain_text
regions.text: "Personally I have been so well pleased with your publication that I have not been able to keep a single copy, but have mailed them to friends all over the country. I shall be glad to continue to show your publication wherever I go. The pleasure that I can give my friends in this way is sufficient reward in itself."

regions.label: plain_text
regions.text: "I have read each successive number of your magazine with increasing satisfaction, and my belief is confirmed that the publication is greatly needed and has possibilities of untold usefulness. The April number came yesterday, with its strikingly beautiful cover page, an artistic advance, I think, on anything that I have ever seen in this particular field heretofore. I am glad to know that your outlook is encouraging. It certainly ought to be." G. S. DICKERMAN.

regions.label: plain_text
regions.text: "I have just had the pleasure of perusing the April number of your splendid magazine and I promptly enclose the price of a subscription. Your work is along the right line and will prove a powerful stimulus not only to the better aspirations of your own people but to the Americanism of all true Americans." HARVEY INGHAM,

regions.label: plain_text
regions.text:
Editor of the Register and Leader,
Des Moines, Ia.

regions.label: plain_text
regions.text: "I want the previous numbers in order that I may get the issue that contains the picture of the 'old colored mother' soliloquizing over her son's lynching. That picture to me is worth the whole price of subscription." GEORGE G. ROSS Denver, Col.
